result.title: Pretraining Data Scale Reverses the Muon-AdamW Fine-Tuning Gap
result.summary: Muon has recently emerged as a promising optimizer for pretraining large language models, offering a speedup over AdamW in minimizing pretraining loss. However, it remains unclear whether Muon's advantage persists after fine-tuning. In this paper, we study the downstream behavior of Muon and AdamW and uncover a surprising trend: beyond a sufficiently large pretraining data budget, AdamW outperforms Muon after fine-tuning. Moreover, as model size increases, AdamW overtakes Muon at progressively smaller pretraining token-parameter ratios. To explain this reversal, we view fine-tuning as a perturbation of the outputs and introduce the margin-to-spread ratio, which measures how far the correct logit lies above the wrong ones relative to how widely the wrong logits are spread. In language models, Muon has the larger margin-to-spread ratio at small data budgets and AdamW at large ones, mirroring the fine-tuning trend. In a linear associative memory, we prove that after one update the margin-to-spread ratio of gradient descent gains on that of Muon as the data budget grows, and simulations show that this trend persists after extended training.

AI.brief_summary: 该文发现预训练数据规模足够大后 AdamW 在微调阶段反超 Muon，并引入「margin-to-spread ratio」刻画正确 logit 相对错误 logit 的领先幅度与散布，在线性联想记忆模型中证明该比值随数据预算增长而向梯度下降倾斜。
AI.relevance_reason: 其 margin-to-spread 指标可作为输出与表示几何的诊断量，可能为刻画 latent 推理状态的判别余量与分布扩散、以及训练预算如何影响 latent 内容可用性提供可供核查的度量思路，但与视觉推理无直接关联。
